scope: Manifest relocation preservation and metadata-only planning inventory
artifact: iris-relocate-collection; optimized Python subprocess from outside repository

requirements.contract: Source fan-in and destination SHA proofs bind ctime and complete file identity; media roots and output mount identity must remain unchanged through publication

Metadata-only inventory and preflight cover all active main/ANN/side-table scoped keys; unmapped scoped paths block root changes, mapped orphan existing/missing vectors survive, and immutable old ledgers are excluded
Repeated primary message associations retain their actual physical sources while nominating the same explicit Iris metadata owner; aliases preserve every competing annotation and ANN payload
Inventory contains only path/stat metadata, is 0600, refuses overwrite, and leaves source versions unchanged
Explicit missing entries retain base rows, original metadata and all ANN vectors with auditable original paths
Existing Iris-only files retain rows and ANN records at preserved destinations without dropping unmapped entries
Every per-chat destination receives a base row and unchanged vector; scalar and real HNSW SQ indexes remain searchable

Changing source versions or the manifest prevents output publication and retains diagnosis-only partial output; published reports retain the exact original captured source versions for post-copy verification
Recovered physical media retains distinct original Iris metadata and vectors without many-to-one key collisions; null optional aliases use the actual source

Explicitly purged or quarantined keys are omitted only from the shadow database with references scrubbed, identical retained files unaffected, and the original source unchanged; blacklist-only or contradictory exclusions are rejected
Many-to-one relocation is explicit opt-in and requires actual old physical size/SHA equivalence; aliases, pHash, absent files and stale source signatures cannot silently prove equivalence

Canonical files remain unique while all typed originals, generation memberships and one-to-many destinations survive; annotation conflicts require an explicit primary and vector conflicts remain searchable under unique variant identities
Historical path/observation events remain immutable across generations; current-generation validation, replay refusal and publication rollback preserve the original source

Exact excluded or explicitly dropped unmapped active main/ANN paths are filtered using path-only metadata before Python payload decoding in both relocation modes; immutable history is copied as opaque Arrow batches and only current-generation observations are decoded for validation
